Phosphine-Catalyzed Stereoselective Tandem Annulation Reaction
for the Synthesis of Chromeno[4,3 ‑b]pyrroles
Zonghao Dai, † Jin Zhu, † Wenbo Su, Wuxian Zeng, Ziqi Liu, Ming Chen, * and Qingfa Zhou *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 7008 −7012 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A phosphine-catalyzed tandem cyclization reaction
has been developed to provide a series of chromeno[4,3- b]pyrrole
derivatives, which contain three consecutive asymmetric centers.
The reaction has a good yield, excellent stereoselectivity, and Z/E
selectivity. The new method is simple, requires only mild
conditions, and shows tolerance for various functional groups.
Similarly, this reaction can be catalyzed by a chiral phosphine
catalyst to achieve asymmetric synthesis.
T
he chromenopyrrole derivatives are ubiquitous structural
options founded in numerous natural and biologically
active compounds ( Figure 1 ).
1,2 For instance, compound a is
an antagonist of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (mAChRs)
and displays potent activity against four selected bacterial
pathogens.
2a Product b forms a lead for the development of
new AChE inhibitors. 2b In addition, chromeno[4,3- b]pyrrole
derivatives were reported to possess anticancer, antimicrobial,
and antioxidant activity.
2c−f Therefore, the development of a
facile and stereoselective me thodology for constructing
chromeno[4,3-b]pyrrole frameworks has been a long-standing
goal in organic and medicinal chemistry.
To date, numerous methodologies for obtaining the
chromenopyrrole have been reported because of their
remarkable biolog ical activities.
3 For example, in 2005,
Geib’s group successfully pioneered a double intramolecular
cyclization of O-allylic salicylaldehydes to synthesize
chromeno[4,3-b]pyrroles ( Scheme 1 ). However, some of
these protocols su ﬀered from some undesired limitations
such as excessive temperatures, toxic solvents, or complex
experimental operations. Considering the huge potential
application value of these compounds in drug discovery,
exploiting expeditious and e ﬃcient methodologies to access
structurally diverse and complex chromeno[4,3- b]pyrroles is
highly desirable. Since the report of Lu ’s [3+2] cycloaddition, a
great deal of research has been devoted to exploring the
cycloaddition reaction catalyzed by organophosphines.
4 These
methods have become sturdy synthetic tools for the
construction of a wide range of carbo- and heterocycles.
5 In
terms of mechanism, phosphine-catalyzed annulations can be
carried out by zwitterions, which were directly formed by 1,4-
addition of a phosphine catalyst to activated allenes. These
zwitterions exhibit excellent dipolar carbon synthon properties

group reported that as a versatile dipolarophile, δ-acetoxy
allenoates had the ability to undergo 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition
reactions with various dipoles.
7a In the presence of a phosphine
catalyst, the allenoates can be turned into 2-phosphonium
diene intermediates, which can react with an array of
bisnucleophiles.
7 Herein, we report a phosphine-catalyzed
cascade cycloaddition reaction between aldimine esters and δ-
acetoxy allenoates, which delivered diastereoselective chrome-
nopyrrole derivatives.
Our investigation began with the screening of the catalysts
for the reaction of aldimine ester 1a and allenoate 2a in
toluene at room temperature ( Table 1 , entries 1 −4). Weakly
nucleophilic phosphines (such as PPh

could not generate 3aa. Then the e ﬀect of the solvent on the
reaction was evaluated (entries 5 −10). Compared with
toluene, other solvents led to decreased yields or even no
target product. Also, temperature has a signi ﬁcant eﬀect on the
yield of 3aa (entries 11−13), and the best result was obtained
when the reaction was performed at 40 °C. The structure of
3aa was undeniably con ﬁrmed by X-ray crystallographic
analyses.
8 The substrate scope of allenoates 2 was checked
for their reaction with substrate 1a under the optimized
reaction conditions as stated in entry 11 of Table 1. As shown
in Scheme 2 , both electron-withdrawing and -donating
substituents could be installed at the para position of the
phenyl rings of allenoates 2, with the corresponding
chromeno[4,3-b]pyrroles ( 3ab−3ah)a ﬀorded in good yields
(61−81%) as single diastereomers. It should be noted that the
ortho position groups on the benzene ring of allenoates
decreased the yield ( 3ai−3ak). Furthermore, when a
naphthalene ring replaced the benzene ring, the reaction still
proceeded normally and gave 3al in 62% yield. However, for
the allenoate with an alkyl substituent, the target compound
cannot be obtained ( 3an).
Next, we explored the range of aldimine esters. Generally, all
of the aldimine esters tested led to the expected products
(Scheme 3 ). The reactions were tolerant of the electron-
withdrawing groups such as halogens and donating functional
groups on the benzene ring. For example, substituents could be
ﬁxed at position 4 of the phenol rings in spite of electronic
properties, with the corresponding compounds a ﬀorded in
medium to good yields ( 3ba−3fa). The site of the substituents
on the benzene ring of the aldimine esters had a weak e ﬀect on
the yield. As shown in Scheme 3, 5-methoxy-substituted and 6-
methoxy-substituted aldimine esters a ﬀorded 3ga in 63% yield
and 3ha in 59% yield. The aldimine ester containing the nitro
group made the reaction worse and gave 3ja in signi ﬁcantly

To recognize these novel processes, ethyl ( E)-2-[(2-
hydroxybenzylide ne)amino]acetate 4 and diethyl ( E)-2-
(benzylideneamino)malonate 5 were prepared and treated
with 2a under our standard condition ( Scheme 4 ). However,
no product was obtained. These results illustrated the necessity
of the hydroxy group and malonate for the annulation reaction.
The hydroxyl at position 2 might activate the malonate and
could form intramolecular hydrogen bonds to stabilize the
azomethine ylide.
9
On the basis of the results of our control experiments and
previous research, we suggested the possible mechanisms of
these domino processes ( Scheme 5 ).
7 Cationic intermediate I
was formed by the addition −elimination reaction of phosphine
and 2. Then the carbanion of II attacked I to generate
zwitterionic intermediate III, which eventually allowed for
intramolecular addition of the carbon anion to vinyl
phosphonium to a ﬀord intermediate IV. After a H-shift
process, the resultant intermediate V might undergo intra-
molecular nucleophilic attack, leading to intermediate VI.
Finally, an elimination yielded product 3 and regenerated the
phosphine catalyst.
In addition, we try to explore the asymmetric version of this
cycloaddition. Although many chiral phosphine catalysts were
investigated, most of them resulted in either a low yield or a
low ee value (see the Supporting Information ). Only chiral
phosphine C10 gave satisfactory results ( Scheme 6 ). It is
particularly worth noting that no matter what phosphine
catalysts were used, the reaction has excellent diastereoselec-
tivity and excellent Z/E selectivity. With C10 as the catalyst,
3aa could be obtained in 75% yield with good enantiose-
lectivity (87% ee) when the reaction was performed in CHCl
3
at 0 °C. With the aim of further improving the
enantioselectivity, we investigated the e ﬀect of the substituent
of allenoates. Pleasingly, a diphenyl methyl-containing alkene
tolerated this reaction, rendering 3am in 76% yield with 91%
ee, 20:1 dr, and 25:1 Z/E (entry 19). Generally, a variety of
allenoates that have di ﬀerent substituents on the benzene ring
performed quite well, giving corresponding products 3ac−3ah
in moderate yields (57 −66%) with good stereoselectivities (all
>20:1 dr, >25:1 Z/E, and 80 −84% ee). Furthermore, allonate
2l could also react with 3a in the presence of C10, giving 3al in
52% yield with 78% ee. Subsequently, both electron-with-
drawing and -donating substituents on the benzene ring of
aldimine esters were found to be tolerant under the optimal
conditions, and products 3bm−3dm can be obtained in
medium to good yields (56 −73%) with good diastereo- and
enantioselectivities (all >20:1 dr, >25:1 Z/E, and 72 −84% ee).
To highlight the synthetic potential of this method, the
transformations of 3 were studied ( Scheme 7). First, treatment

b]pyrrole 3bm underwent an e ﬀective coupling reaction and
provided azepine 7 in 71% yield.

In conclusion, we have developed a phosphine-catalyzed
cascade cycloaddition strategy for facily synthesizing chrome-
nopyrrole derivatives from aldimine esters and δ-acetoxy
allenoates. In particular, a wide range of products have been
aﬀorded in generally good yields with excellent diastereose-
lectivities. In addition, by using a chiral phosphine catalyst, the
cycloaddition reaction can also initially realize the asymmetric
synthesis of chromeno[4,3- b]pyrrole. This protocol can be
expected to ﬁnd wide synthetic application because of its
simple operation, mild reaction conditions, high e ﬃciency, and
high chemo- and enantioselectivity.
